fields.explanation: For every integer k≥4 take t=a=3, x=1^k, f(x)=1^3∘2^(k−3), and p0=(1−1/k)^k>0. These satisfy a<k and a≥t. The difference between the two displayed bounds is 4p0/(k−1)²>0; k=1001 is one example. The selected Lean theorem also holds algebraically at k=3, but that endpoint is outside this source proof branch.
fields.flaw: The proof asserts that (1+2/(k-1))^(a-1) is at most 1+2(a-1)/(k-1), an inequality used to establish Part 1's upper bound in the Non-Intersection Bias Lemma.
